transport: 2-wire maintained dry contact (black/white wires of the supplied Control Harness) · open-circuit voltage on the input: ? (not stated) · current through a closed contact: ? (not stated) · polarity: none stated for the control pair; module power is red (+)/black (−) to the generator battery (p6–7); fusing: a 5 A fuse ships in the kit (p2) and "Start Module internal contacts are fused with the start module main fuse. Additional circuit protection may be required" (p7); ignition switch: "MUST be left on for the 2-wire start to operate. This puts the generator in standby mode and will not drain the battery" (p7); temperature: choke actuator "-20C - 60C. It is not recommended to start the generator with the remote start outside this range. Choke actuator failure may result" (p7); fob: Standard kit has none.

models.name: Honda EU3000is (EU3000is1)
models.rating: 2.8 kVA rated / 3.0 kVA max, gasoline, electric start yes (12 V 8.6 Ah battery)
models.notes: Honda OM 00X31ZS96120 p82; factory choke is a manual knob, so the kit adds a choke actuator

gotchas: "Closing the circuit between the black and white wires of the Control Harness will start the generator and opening the circuit will shut it off" (p7). Nothing about a run-confirm output, crank duration, or retry count — the module is a black box.
The module unplugs and replaces the Honda ignition-switch connector (step 4); Honda's EU3000is has no factory remote connector at all (no "remote" anywhere in the OM).

The "MUST be left on" requirement contradicts Honda's OM p34: "Do not leave the engine switch in the ON position when the generator is not operating as the battery will discharge." GenStart claims its standby mode avoids the drain; unmeasured.

Premium (wireless) variant, https://genstart.ca/uploads/3/4/9/7/34974774/manual_eu3000is_premium_wireless_start_pdf_new_gear_actuator_v2.pdf: same 2-wire module plus 1000 m transmitter; "The 2-wire system will operate with the WIRELESS START SYSTEM SWITCH 'OFF'" and the wireless receiver "will drain the battery in a few days" (p9). Whether opening the 2-wire contact stops a fob-started engine is **not stated**.

Honda's Oil Alert stops the engine with the switch left ON (OM, "Oil Alert" section) — the contact stays closed, so the controller must detect the stop itself. Proof of running at the panel is what catches it.
